To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the system can verify moving objects in airborne video sequences using a novel view of the testing object at a pose that matches that of the testing object in the frame; and (2) the use of both color and spatial information in the matching process, combined with the use of a weighted average rule for combining the color and spatial match scores, provides a robust method for matching moving objects in video sequences.

(a) using a homography-based method to generate novel views of exemplar images is a simple, efficient, and effective approach to handling appearance change due to pose variation; (b) a combination of rotationally invariant color and spatial-feature matching provides robust performance for moving object verification, and (c) temporal analysis of the match scores is an effective way to improve the performance of moving object verification in video.
